papers.title: Left Bundle-Branch Area Pacing vs Right Ventricular Pacing for Atrioventricular Block and Preserved Left Ventricular Function: The LEAP-Block Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: Randomised trial in 14 Chinese hospitals of 499 patients with atrioventricular block, preserved ejection fraction and expected ventricular pacing above 40%. Left bundle-branch area pacing cut 24-month death, heart failure events or biventricular upgrade versus right ventricular pacing (2.4% vs 12.5%; HR 0.37), with fewer heart failure events and similar complications.
papers.short_title: the LEAP-Block trial of left bundle-branch area pacing versus right ventricular pacing

papers.title: Interpreting High-Sensitivity Cardiac Troponin in Clinical Practice and Emerging Directions: Detection Is No Longer Diagnosis.
papers.summary: This narrative review by Spanos and Januzzi argues that high-sensitivity troponin has made detecting myocardial injury easy but classifying it hard, leading to overdiagnosis of secondary infarction and dismissal of chronic injury. It offers bedside guidance on assay properties, rapid ESC rule-out algorithms, the Fifth Universal Definition and other causes of troponin elevation.

papers.title: Beyond HFmrEF: New Classification, Unchanged Treatment Evidence.
papers.summary: No abstract was available for this paper, so no results are reported here. Judging from its title and keywords, it examines how heart failure with mildly reduced ejection fraction is being reclassified, and holds that the treatment evidence itself is unchanged. See the full paper in JACC for the details and arguments.
